teams.heading: Fiji Rugby keeps watching Mark Nawaqanitawase's switch as Wallabies wait to year-end
teams.body: Today's searches return headlines but no new statement on Mark Nawaqanitawase's eligibility. Fiji Rugby chief executive Koli Sewabu says the union is following a possible switch with interest, while Wallabies coach Les Kiss said: 'I'll wait until the end of the year to see where he sits.' The winger, with 11 Wallabies caps, is eligible for Fiji, Italy and Australia after a three-year stand-down, so Fiji's pitch stays open for the 2027 World Cup.

lead.why: It is the only open Fiji thread with a named player, and today's searches added no new statement, so the edition says so plainly.

teams.heading: Wallabies could knock England out of fifth with Sydney Bledisloe win
teams.body: England's grip on fifth in the World Rugby rankings is under threat from Australia, who were beaten 50-19 by New Zealand at Eden Park last weekend. Planet Rugby's projections, based on the table as of 16 October, have England on 85.68 and Australia on 84.89. A Wallabies win over the All Blacks in Sydney's second Bledisloe Test would lift Australia, coached by Les Kiss, above England, and a margin of more than 15 points would put them fourth, ahead of France.

lead.why: It is a new men's story that bears directly on England's own place in the World Rugby rankings, and nothing else on the shortlist is both new and men's.

teams.heading: French prosecutors open probe into death of Lions lock Hyron Andrews
teams.body: A French investigation is under way into the death of Hyron Andrews, 31, a lock with Johannesburg club Lions, who was found unresponsive at the team hotel on Île de Ré. La Rochelle prosecutor Arnaud Laraize confirmed the inquiry to AFP, and investigators are treating the case as a suspected accident, with an autopsy to follow. Lions will still play Saturday's Champions Cup match against La Rochelle, with a minute's silence before every Champions Cup and Challenge Cup match this weekend.

lead.why: The highest-scoring new item, and a French investigation into a death at a Champions Cup team hotel in France is the story a fan would pass on, even though it is a club story.

teams.heading: Munster name Avan Lee interim chief executive as Ian Flanagan steps down
teams.body: Munster have named New Zealander Avan Lee as interim chief executive, a development first reported on 3 October, replacing Ian Flanagan, who is stepping down after recent criticism. Lee, a former Hurricanes chief executive, wants a role for Peter O'Mahony, according to reports. Munster confirmed Flanagan's departure in a statement, and because Lee's role is interim, the permanent succession remains open.

teams.heading: Ben Thomas set to miss Wales's Nations Championship start with calf injury
teams.body: Cardiff centre Ben Thomas is set to miss the start of Wales's Nations Championship with a calf injury, a blow for head coach Steve Tandy before the opening match against Japan. The 27-year-old, who has 19 caps, started at inside centre in the 43-0 defeat to South Africa in Durban in July. Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl said: "He'll be able to definitely form part of the Nations Championship, but might not recover for the first or second game."

lead.why: Hard injury news for Wales's men's senior side, and it is the most useful item on the shortlist for a fan.

teams.heading: Len Ikitau out with concussion as Declan Meredith starts at 10
teams.body: Wallabies coach Les Kiss has been forced into a reshuffle for Australia's second Bledisloe Cup Test against New Zealand at Accor Stadium. Wallaby Len Ikitau is out with a concussion and Ben Donaldson was hurt in the build-up, so Declan Meredith starts at fly-half and Joseph-Aukuso Sua'ali'i moves back into the centres, with Harry Potter coming into the midfield. Ewen McKenzie, the former Wallabies head coach, said on the Rugby Unity podcast that Kiss' "hands have been forced", while admitting he was still baffled by some of the calls.

lead.why: Concrete selection and injury news for the Wallabies' second Bledisloe Test, with a former coach's criticism attached, rather than a rankings permutation or prediction already covered.

teams.heading: Leroy Carter's ankle, Segner and Aumua concussions hit All Blacks before Sydney
teams.body: All Blacks coach Dave Rennie's side go to Accor Stadium in Sydney for the second Bledisloe Cup Test with a longer injury list than they arrived with in Auckland. Leroy Carter's ankle went as he scored, Anton Segner and Asafo Aumua are concussed after clashing heads in the same tackle, and Ethan Blackadder and Fehi Fineanganofo are out as well. Ardie Savea, Ruben Love and Luke Jacobson were already without for the year. Australia have their own problems at fly-half and centre.

lead.why: It is the freshest hard news in the pack, with new concussion and ankle injuries to All Blacks players ahead of the second Bledisloe Cup Test.

teams.heading: Frans Malherbe reports improvement after long absence, hopes to scrum soon
teams.body: Springbok tighthead Frans Malherbe says his recovery from chronic neck and back problems is going well, with team training without contact now under way at the Stormers. He has not played since March 2025, and on the Boks Unpacked X The Verdict show he said: "I will hopefully soon get stuck into a scrum." The Stormers have left him out of their 2026/27 URC squad, and director of rugby John Dobson has suggested a decision on his future could drag into the new year.

lead.why: It is a new men's Springboks availability story, the strongest hard-news item in the pack, and it is about a player rather than opinion.
